# EMF+ format fixtures

`wine-path.emf` is an original fixture generated by this repository's
`generate-wine.c` using Wine's GDI+ implementation. It contains a cubic path,
a solid fill, and a dashed pen, with a clear and pixel page units. It is an
independent encoder reference, not a Windows-native rendering reference.
The generator, validator, and generated Wine fixture use this repository's
GPL-2.0-or-later license; no Wine implementation source was copied.

Regenerate on Linux with Wine development headers:

```sh
winegcc crates/krkr_plugin/tests/fixtures/layer_ex_draw/generate-wine.c -o /tmp/layerexdraw-record-reference -lgdiplus
WINEDEBUG=-all /tmp/layerexdraw-record-reference.exe
cp /tmp/layerexdraw-external.emf crates/krkr_plugin/tests/fixtures/layer_ex_draw/wine-path.emf
```

`wine-mixed.emf` exercises a linear gradient, an excluded clip rectangle,
positioned text and a compressed bitmap. Wine records the text as
`EmfPlusDrawDriverString`. The separate DrawString test constructs a formatted
text record with the object layouts in
[MS-EMFPLUS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/ae7927c3-e416-4069-a9b8-3200113d6c41).

```sh
winegcc crates/krkr_plugin/tests/fixtures/layer_ex_draw/generate-mixed.c -o /tmp/layerexdraw-mixed-reference -lgdiplus
WINEDEBUG=-all /tmp/layerexdraw-mixed-reference.exe
cp /tmp/layerexdraw-mixed.emf crates/krkr_plugin/tests/fixtures/layer_ex_draw/wine-mixed.emf
```

`ms-emfplus-path.bin` contains the exact 196-byte hexadecimal path-object
record from Microsoft [MS-EMFPLUS] v20240423, section 3.2.32.21 (pages 221–222).
Its unit test also consumes the literal FillPath bytes from section 3.2.32.22.
The sample has 19 points, including five cubic segments, and a close flag.
Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/
Microsoft's Open Specifications copyright notice permits distributing portions
of the documentation needed to implement or document the specified technology.
The bytes are a protocol example, not third-party parser source.

`validate-wine.c` opens the original path fixture and the Rust export in
Wine GDI+. The validator checks every playback status, counts the exported
path and drawing records, and compares the two 64×48 pixel buffers. Run it
in a graphical Linux session with Wine development tools:

```sh
cargo test -p krkr_plugin --lib wine_gdiplus_plays_exported_metafile -- --ignored --nocapture
```

Wine 11.22 plays all 18 records in the exported path sample, including two
paths, one brush, one pen and two drawing records. All 3,072 pixels match.
Continued-object tests use records constructed from the specification.
